title: Unions Can Save Tech Workers and Tech Work
excerpt: Two University of California tech workers explain their unionization process — and how unions can help recapture the original promise of tech being used to better people’s lives rather than make the worst people in the world ever richer.
content_html:
A dramatic shift has taken place in the tech industry over the last several years. Industry leaders who once had a reputation as innovative forward thinkers are more familiar as misanthropic paranoiacs. The playful atmosphere of tech offices flush with investment, enjoying luxe catered lunches to attract programming talent, has been replaced by a looming fear that layoffs are just around the corner as artificial intelligence (AI) company executives make repeated public statements that any day now, everyone will be replaced by superintelligent chatbots. The once-sage advice to “learn to code” isn’t heard much these days.

One could hardly be blamed for feeling pessimistic about the tech industry. But last May, 2,100 information technology employees at the University of California (UC) voted to join the union of University Professional and Technical Employees (UPTE-CWA Local 9119). Among the reasons for joining, members have pointed to the layoff protections the union won in its last contract, as well as the positive social vision of technology for which organized workers can fight.

This was the largest effort to organize technology workers in the history of the US labor movement. While the tech industry might still be new ground for unions, the methods it took to win were familiar as ever. Jacobin contributor and tech worker Aaron Petcoff spoke with Local 9119 President Dan Russell and University of California, Los Angeles (UCLA) Unit Cochair Max Belasco about the campaign, what it took to win, and how workers can organize to build technology that serves people rather than the bosses.

content_html_zh:
过去几年，科技行业发生了巨大的转变。 曾经被誉为创新型前瞻性思想家的行业领导者，现在更多地被认为是厌世的偏执狂。 科技办公室充满投资、享受豪华午餐以吸引编程人才的有趣氛围，已经被一种迫在眉睫的担忧所取代，即随着人工智能 (AI) 公司高管多次公开声明，每个人都将被超级智能聊天机器人取代，裁员即将来临。 如今，“学习编码”这个曾经神圣的建议已经很少被听到了。

人们对科技行业感到悲观是无可厚非的。 但去年 5 月，加州大学 (UC) 的 2,100 名信息技术员工投票加入大学专业技术员工工会 (UPTE-CWA Local 9119)。 在加入的原因中，成员们指出了工会在上一份合同中赢得的裁员保护，以及有组织的工人可以为之奋斗的积极的技术社会愿景。

这是美国劳工运动历史上组织技术工人的最大规模的努力。 尽管科技行业可能仍是工会的新领域，但工会获胜所采取的方法却一如既往地熟悉。 雅各宾派撰稿人和技术工作者 Aaron Petcoff 与 Local 9119 主席 Dan Russell 和加州大学洛杉矶分校 (UCLA) 部门联合主席 Max Belasco 讨论了该活动、获胜所需的条件，以及工人们如何组织起来开发为人民而不是老板服务的技术。
